paper_metadata.title: CALPHAD informed design of multicomponent CoNiCr-based superalloys exhibiting large lattice misfit and high yield stress

evidence.quote: In this work, new L12-phase hardened, low-density CoNiCr-based superalloys were developed with the assistance of CALPHAD calculations.
In the Co–Al–W system, the large amount of W required to stabilize γ′ precipitates increases the density to unacceptably high values (>9.5 g/cm3) compared to Ni-based superalloys [5].

New low-density γ′ strengthened CoNiCr-based superalloys were developed with the assistance of the CALPHAD method and transition temperatures, microstructures, lattice misfits and mechanical properties were characterized.

evidence.section: 4.2. The γ′ precipitate strengthening at high temperature
evidence.quote: According to a simplified model for coherency stress calculation [47], the coherency stress contribution can be expressed by Δσcoherent = Vγ′ δ E[100], where E[100] should be the elastic modulus of the γ matrix.
